title: Retrospective A/B Promoter with Graceful Shadow Sweep and Rollback Oracle
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Introduces a retrospective promotion mode for A/B experiments, a shadow-sweep validator for delayed promotions, and a rollback oracle that leverages replayed shadow traces and differential metrics to auto-suggest backouts.
description:
Motivation: Some experiments require a delayed promotion decision because short-lived canaries miss user-surface regressions that only appear after longer interaction. This PR adds a "retrospective" promotion mode that keeps the candidate in shadow for a configurable observation window, runs deterministic replays and differential metrics, and only promotes once the retrospective checks pass. It also includes a 'graceful shadow sweep' to gradually drain shadow traffic and a 'rollback oracle' that flags likely regressions using replayed traces, token-level deltas, and multi-metric heuristics.

What changed (high level): added a new rollout policy mode "retrospective_promote"; implemented a retrospective engine that (1) captures shadow traces, (2) replays them through candidate and baseline under identical seeds and context, (3) computes a set of differential metrics (latency delta, perplexity delta, functional failure rate, hallucination signals), and (4) applies configurable gates (thresholds + statistical tests) before promoting. Added an automated rollback oracle that computes a confidence score for regressions and surfaces remediation suggestions in the rollout UI and telemetry.

APIs/config: rollout spec gains an optional "retrospective_policy" block (fields: retrospective_window_minutes, evaluation_backfill_minutes, min_shadow_samples, statistical_test: (ks|wilcoxon|bootstrap), promotion_signature, sweep_rate). Example: "retrospective_policy": {"retrospective_window_minutes": 60, "min_shadow_samples": 2000, "statistical_test": "bootstrap", "sweep_rate": 0.15}. Existing canary/ab flows continue to work; this is opt-in.

Design notes: the retrospective engine uses the existing offline-replay harness but extends it to support live-cohort sampling and deterministic replays with fixed KV cache seeds. To keep runtime isolation, capture payloads are stored in an S3-like object store with TTL and are encrypted with KMS. The rollback oracle is a lightweight model that scores multi-metric deviations and produces a human-readable explanation (top contributing metrics).

Operational behavior and SLOs: the retrospective window is bounded to avoid unbounded shadow retention; default max retention is 72 hours. The promotion decision path is synchronous for operators (promote button) and can be automated when all gates pass. The sweep drains shadow lanes at the configured sweep_rate to minimize user-facing risk during final promote.

Testing and rollout: unit tests for the replay harness and statistical gating; integration tests that run a 10k-sample synthetic shadow feed in CI (takes ~7 minutes). Added a local-mode tester in perf-canary to simulate retrospective flows. Staging rollout was run against a sampled internal traffic slice for 48 hours before merge.

Backward compatibility and migration: rollout specs without retrospective_policy are unchanged. For customers who use bespoke rollout controllers, we publish a migration guide and a converter script that translates existing canary configs to a safe retrospective template.

Security & privacy: captured traces are redacted by the existing PII-scrubber before storage. KMS encryption is enforced for object store buckets used by the retrospective engine.

Operator runbook (summary): 1) Create rollout with retrospective_policy; 2) observe shadow metrics in Console under "Retrospective" tab; 3) run replay verification (button) or wait for automated evaluation; 4) promote when gates clear or follow rollback oracle suggestions; 5) if invoked, rollback oracle creates an incident suggestion with top metric deltas and recommended rollback temperament.

This PR is intentionally scoped to the orchestration, telemetry, and replay pieces. Serving-side kernels were not modified.
